sections.headline: A Full-Spectrum Design Practice

items.title: Urban Research & Diagnostics
items.description: We begin every engagement with a rigorous site analysis: pedestrian counts, behavioral observation, environmental sensing, and stakeholder interviews to establish a quantified baseline.

items.title: Community Engagement & Data Synthesis
items.description: Structured participatory processes — surveys, workshops, and co-design sessions — generate qualitative data that is coded, weighted, and integrated alongside quantitative findings.

items.title: Evidence-Based Concept Design
items.description: Design proposals are generated directly from research outputs. Every spatial decision is traceable to a data point, ensuring defensible, community-aligned outcomes.

items.title: Environmental Performance Analysis
items.description: We model microclimate, solar access, acoustic conditions, and stormwater performance to optimize comfort, resilience, and ecological value across all seasons.

items.title: Implementation Documentation
items.description: Detailed construction documentation, material specifications, and phasing strategies ensure design intent is preserved through procurement and build.

items.title: Post-Occupancy Evaluation
items.description: We return after opening to measure real-world performance against projected metrics, generating a feedback loop that sharpens every future project.

sections.intent: Address common questions from municipal and institutional clients to reduce friction in the inquiry process and pre-qualify expectations.
sections.headline: What Clients Ask Before Engaging

items.title: What types of clients do you typically work with?
items.description: We work primarily with municipal governments, public development authorities, urban regeneration agencies, and civic-minded private developers. Our projects range from neighborhood pocket parks to major metropolitan infrastructure.

items.title: How long does a typical project take?
items.description: Project timelines vary by scope. A focused urban diagnostic study may take 6–10 weeks, while a full design and documentation engagement for a major public space typically runs 12–24 months.

items.title: Can you work within existing procurement frameworks?
items.description: Yes. We have experience operating within public tender processes, design competitions, and direct commission frameworks across multiple jurisdictions.

items.title: Do you collaborate with other architects or engineers?
items.description: Frequently. We operate as lead design consultant or as a specialist collaborator within larger multidisciplinary teams, depending on project structure.

sections.intent: Communicate the founding story and studio values to give prospective clients a sense of shared purpose and long-term commitment to civic design.
sections.headline: Founded on a Frustration with Guesswork
sections.subheadline: Axiom Public Lab was built on the belief that public space design deserved the same analytical rigor applied to infrastructure engineering.
sections.body: In 2009, Dr. Nadia Osei watched a newly opened plaza in Rotterdam sit almost entirely empty within six months of opening — despite winning a design award. The problem wasn't aesthetics. It was that nobody had measured how people actually moved through that part of the city before designing it. Axiom Public Lab was founded the following year with a single operating principle: every design decision must be traceable to evidence. Fifteen years later, that principle drives every project, every hire, and every method we develop.
